items.title: An AI-generated daily quiz app I built on my bike
items.raw_excerpt: Not a startup attempt, just a weekend project for my family. My parents do a daily quiz, but the site they use looks like it was built in 1999 and not touched since. I thought it’d be a fun excuse to rebuild something simple and leverage AI for automation. The app uses 5 agents to generate a 10 question general knowledge quiz, daily, with loose association to a random topic. It also allows for user generated quizzes based on a provided topic. Side note: I built the majority of it whilst riding my indoor bike. Claude Code + WisprFlow is insanely good these days.

title_i18n.en: An AI-generated daily quiz app I built on my bike
title_i18n.zh: 我在骑行途中开发了一款AI生成每日问答应用。
title_i18n.es: Una aplicación de cuestionario diario generada por IA que construí en mi bicicleta.

excerpt_i18n.en: Not a startup attempt, just a weekend project for my family. My parents do a daily quiz, but the site they use looks like it was built in 1999 and not touched since. I thought it’d be a fun excuse to rebuild something simple and leverage AI for automation. The app uses 5 agents to generate a 10 question general knowledge quiz, daily, with loose association to a random topic. It also allows for user generated quizzes based on a provided topic. Side note: I built the majority of it whilst riding my indoor bike. Claude Code + WisprFlow is insanely good these days.
excerpt_i18n.zh: 并非创业尝试，仅为家人打造的周末项目。我父母每天做小测验，但他们使用的网站看起来像是1999年建成后就再未更新过。我觉得这是个有趣的理由，可以借此机会重新构建一个更现代的版本。
excerpt_i18n.es: No es un intento de startup, solo un proyecto de fin de semana para mi familia. Mis padres hacen un concurso diario, pero la página que usan parece construida en 1999 y sin tocar desde entonces. Pensé que sería una excusa divertida para reconstruir algo así.

items.title: AceIQ360 – First AI memory system to achieve 100% on LongMemEval
items.raw_excerpt:
I built AceIQ360, a deterministic agentic memory system. Results:
- LongMemEval: 100% (500/500) - first ever
- LoCoMo: 75.32% J-Score (vs Mem0 68.44%) - 80x cheaper per turn
- 13x faster Built on RudraDB, my relationship-aware vector database with automatic relationship detection. No LLM extraction calls. Pure embedding-based. Solo developer. Looking for feedback.

title_i18n.en: AceIQ360 – First AI memory system to achieve 100% on LongMemEval
title_i18n.zh: AceIQ360——首个在长记忆评估中实现100%准确率的AI记忆系统。
title_i18n.es: AceIQ360 – Primer sistema de memoria de IA en lograr el 100% en LongMemEval

excerpt_i18n.en:
I built AceIQ360, a deterministic agentic memory system. Results:
- LongMemEval: 100% (500/500) - first ever
- LoCoMo: 75.32% J-Score (vs Mem0 68.44%) - 80x cheaper per turn
- 13x faster Built on RudraDB, my relationship-aware vector database with automatic relationship detection. No LLM extraction calls. Pure embedding-based. Solo developer. Looking for feedback.
excerpt_i18n.zh:
我开发了AceIQ360，一个确定性智能记忆系统。成果如下：
- LongMemEval：100%（500/500）——首次实现
- LoCoMo：75.32% J分数（对比Mem0的68.44%）——每轮成本降低80倍

items.title: Change my mind) should AI coding conversations be append-only?
items.raw_excerpt: I work on an open-source coding agent, and one design choice we made is to keep conversations append-only. No editing past prompts. Many would argue this feels restrictive. Isn’t it just better to edit an earlier message or tweak the prompt and move on? And this is what most coding agents allow, and on the front, it looks convenient. But realistically, editing conversation history throws away the most valuable signal you have. When you edit the past prompts, it's basically erasing the part on how the agent actually reasoned. You lose the failed attempts, the wrong assumptions, the dead ends, and the recovery steps. That history is exactly what you need to understand why something worked or didn’t. items.title: Why delegation beats memory in AI Agents
items.raw_excerpt: We've spent the last 6 months building Seer, an agent engine for enterprise workflows. We’re launching on NYE, but honestly, we’re still in the trenches. While scanning the space, I keep seeing devs (us included, initially) get obsessed with complex "memory" layers and graph-based reflection. In practice, we found they mostly lead to context poisoning and high latency. We pivoted to a "Barbell Strategy": Crisp, lean inter-agent instructions paired with massive, localized "artifact" context for sub-agents that are immediately killed after the task. I’m curious—for those of you building agents in production: Have you found a way to make "long-term memory" actually reliable, or are you also moving toward ephemeral, specialized agents? I’m Sergio, the founder of LynxPrompt: https://lynxprompt.com I built it because I got tired of rewriting the same “how I want the AI to code” rules every time I started a new repo. LynxPrompt generates and manages AI coding rules/config files in a portable way across IDEs and other AI-enabled coding tools. It also lets you save, share & discover blueprints (also called templates/AI configs/prompts — the industry has many names for these) made by other devs. Honestly, I know: yet another AI tool. But my problem was very specific: keeping AI coding rules consistent across projects and tools without relying too much on “memory” features. items.title: AI can help get fusion from lab to energy grid by the 2030s – WEF
items.raw_excerpt: The World Economic Forum reports that AI could accelerate the commercialization of fusion energy, potentially helping fusion power reach the grid by the 2030s through optimization of reactor designs and plasma behavior prediction.

title_i18n.en: AI can help get fusion from lab to energy grid by the 2030s – WEF
title_i18n.zh: 人工智能有望在2030年代前将核聚变从实验室推向能源电网——世界经济论坛。
title_i18n.es: La IA puede ayudar a llevar la fusión del laboratorio a la red eléctrica para la década de 2030 – Foro Económico Mundial

excerpt_i18n.en: The World Economic Forum reports that AI could accelerate the commercialization of fusion energy, potentially helping fusion power reach the grid by the 2030s through optimization of reactor designs and plasma behavior prediction.
excerpt_i18n.zh: 世界经济论坛报告指出，人工智能技术有望加速核聚变能源的商业化进程，帮助核聚变技术从实验室走向电网。通过优化反应堆设计、预测等离子体行为和加速材料研发，AI可能推动核聚变能源在2030年代实现并网发电。

items.title: Practical AI setup for staying on top of personal messages?
items.raw_excerpt:
End-of-year reflection: I’ve let messages pile up, and I want a sustainable way to maintain the relationships I care about. Most of my personal backlog is on iPhone/iMessage, and I’m looking for a mobile-first system. I’m also juggling work + personal logistics, so I need something that works in short batches vs. being “always on”. I’m looking for success/failure stories and practical setups using AI for triage + drafting across texts/email/voicemail. I’m not looking to auto-send replies—just help deciding what to reply to and drafting something I’ll send myself. Questions I’d love input on: - What workflow finally stuck (batching, queues, reminders, templates, “SLA” rules)?

items.title: So Long, GPT-5. Hello, Qwen
items.raw_excerpt: In the AI boom, chatbots and GPTs come and go quickly. (Remember Llama?) GPT-5 had a big year, but 2026 will be all about Qwen.

title_i18n.en: So Long, GPT-5. Hello, Qwen
title_i18n.zh: 再见，GPT-5。你好，Qwen。
title_i18n.es: Adiós, GPT-5. Hola, Qwen.

excerpt_i18n.en: In the AI boom, chatbots and GPTs come and go quickly. (Remember Llama?) GPT-5 had a big year, but 2026 will be all about Qwen.
excerpt_i18n.zh: 在人工智能热潮中，聊天机器人与GPT模型更迭迅速。（还记得Llama吗？）GPT-5今年表现抢眼，但2026年将是通义千问的主场。
excerpt_i18n.es: En el auge de la IA, los chatbots y los GPT van y vienen rápidamente. (¿Recuerdas Llama?) GPT-5 tuvo un gran año, pero 2026 será el año de Qwen.
